chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from one of his companions, from Mufazzal ibn Umar who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'If you are able, do not sleep at night until you seek Refuge with eleven Letters (Phrases).' I said, 'Inform me with them.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Say.'

'I seek Refuge with the Might of Allah, and I seek Refuge with the Power of Allah, and I seek Refuge with the Majesty of Allah, and I seek Refuge with the Authority of Allah, and I seek Refuge with the Beauty of Allah, and I seek Refuge with the Defence of Allah, and I seek Refuge with the Prevention of Allah, and I seek Refuge with the Grip of Allah, and I seek Refuge with the Kingdom of Allah, and I seek Refuge with the Face of Allah, and I seek Refuge with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) from the evil of what He Created, Spread, and Settled. And seek Refuge with it whenever you desire.'
ai.seo_question: What is the supplication to recite before sleeping according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) prescribes this specific dhikr, invoking eleven divine attributes such as 'Izzah' (Majesty) and 'Jalal' (Glory), to seek protection from the evil of created beings before sleep. This practice reflects the Shia emphasis on utilizing the names and attributes of Allah as a spiritual shield, aligning with the concept of 'Tawassul' through divine qualities. The inclusion of 'Rasulullah' highlights the intercessory role of the Prophet in seeking refuge, a key element in Shia devotional theology.
